cases.claim: ThingId remains the lookup key when private Godot bindings are destroyed and recreated.
NodePath, RID, ResourceUID and transport/process handles are rejected from the target projection fixture.
A semantic-only Thing can have zero Godot bindings without ceasing to exist.
Sparse facet realization creates engine objects only for requested private target facets.
Node-per-Thing realization remains a measured comparison candidate, not a canonical identity rule.
Scene-subtree realization remains a measured comparison candidate, not a canonical ownership rule.
Central scheduler bridge orders semantic work by explicit SplashMX keys rather than SceneTree callback order.
Reversing engine/event arrival insertion order produces the same semantic activation trace.
Unsupported required target features fail before binding activation.
Unsupported optional target features may be omitted without rewriting canonical project data.
Headless profile can omit render/audio/input bindings while preserving the same semantic fixture revision.
Web and native export profiles consume the same spike source and semantic fixture contract.
Representative render path uses private Node2D bindings only.
Representative physics path uses private Area2D/CollisionShape2D bindings only.
Representative audio path uses a private AudioStreamPlayer binding only.
Representative input is normalized into scheduler work rather than becoming durable device identity.
Protected Asset projection carries only exact AssetId plus immutable revision digest and cannot field-mix source/audio/provenance metadata.
Binding recreation preserves the exact protected Asset revision reference.
Creation, churn, scheduler, object-count and memory metrics are emitted from real Godot 4.7.2 execution.
Runtime startup is measured separately as headless process launch-to-exit evidence.
Measured timings are evidence for the named CI environment, not universal target SLOs.
Selection prefers the sparse-facet layout only after semantic and adversarial gates pass.
The selected layout may use zero, one or multiple private engine objects per Thing.
No Godot binding object is serialized back into the production core or protected-media revision.
